inputs.original_proposal: Review: coalesced signal updates with LiveView Page v0.3.0 phase 2

blockers: Thread safety violation in onFrame(): The in-flight frame backpressure mechanism (m_inFlightFrames atomic counter with MaxInFlightFrames limit) has been removed. Without this limit, QMetaObject::invokeMethod with Qt::QueuedConnection can accumulate unbounded items in the event queue, leading to memory exhaustion or severe lag when frames arrive faster than GUI thread processing. Line ~114-140 in qttunebridge.cpp shows the new code only checks m_currentFrameCount (non-atomic) without any queued-item limit.

Data race in m_currentFrameCount: The member variable m_currentFrameCount is accessed non-atomically in onFrame() for the backpressure check and non-atomically incremented in handleFrameInternal(). This creates a data race between the worker thread (reading for check) and GUI thread (writing increment).

Removed test coverage: The test 'StreamingContinuesPastTenThousandFrames' in test_bridge.cpp was specifically designed to verify backpressure behavior and prevent the freeze bug. Its removal eliminates regression testing for this critical safety mechanism.
questions: Is the removal of SignalListModel intentional as part of a larger refactoring? This represents a significant reduction in functionality (live signal display, subscription management, signal decoding).

What is the migration path for signal decoding? The old code used qttune_decode_signal() with a hardcoded 8-byte length, but qttune_frame_t.data[64] suggests CAN-FD support. Is signal decoding being moved to a different layer?
nits: m_currentFrameCount should be std::atomic<int> if used for synchronization between threads
The comment 'frame is stack-owned by mock_worker' in onFrame() is now stale since signal decoding was removed - the frame copy is still needed for thread safety but the comment should be updated
Consider adding a TODO or documentation about why SignalListModel was removed if this is temporary
